source.text: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֗וֹשׁ לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס דָּבָר֙ נִגְלָ֣ה לְדָֽנִיֵּ֔אל אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר וֶאֱמֶ֤ת הַדָּבָר֙ וְצָבָ֣א גָד֔וֹל וּבִין֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֔ר וּבִ֥ינָה ל֖וֹ בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In year three of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and true [was] the word, and a great conflict; and he understood the word, and understanding [was] to him in the vision.

en.L: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. And the word was true, and [it concerned] a great conflict. And he understood the word and had understanding of the vision.
en.B: In the third year of the reign of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was made known to Daniel, who had been given the name Belteshazzar. The message was true, and it was about a great war. He understood the message; he was given understanding in the vision.
en.R: In Cyrus's third year as king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was also called Belteshazzar. The message was true. It was about a great war. Daniel understood the message. He understood what the vision meant.

fr.L: La troisième année de Cyrus, roi de Perse, une parole fut révélée à Daniel, dont le nom était Beltshatsar. Et la parole [était] vraie, et [elle concernait] un grand combat. Et il comprit la parole et eut l’intelligence de la vision.
fr.B: La troisième année du règne de Cyrus, roi de Perse, un message fut révélé à Daniel, qu’on avait appelé Beltshatsar. Ce message était vrai, et il annonçait une grande guerre. Daniel comprit le message ; l’intelligence lui fut donnée dans la vision.
fr.R: Cyrus était roi de Perse depuis trois ans quand un message a été révélé à Daniel, qu’on appelait aussi Beltshatsar. Ce message était vrai. Il parlait d’une grande guerre. Daniel a compris le message. Il a compris ce que la vision voulait dire.

es.L: En el año tercero de Ciro, rey de Persia, fue revelada una palabra a Daniel, cuyo nombre era llamado Beltsasar. Y la palabra [era] verdadera, y [se refería a] un gran conflicto. Y él entendió la palabra, y tuvo entendimiento de la visión.
es.B: En el tercer año del reinado de Ciro, rey de Persia, se le dio a conocer un mensaje a Daniel, a quien habían puesto el nombre de Beltsasar. El mensaje era verdadero y trataba de una gran guerra. Daniel entendió el mensaje; se le dio entendimiento en la visión.
es.R: Cuando Ciro llevaba tres años como rey de Persia, se le reveló un mensaje a Daniel, a quien también llamaban Beltsasar. El mensaje era verdadero. Trataba de una gran guerra. Daniel entendió el mensaje. Entendió lo que significaba la visión.

sw.L: Katika mwaka wa tatu wa Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, neno lilifunuliwa kwa Danieli, aliyeitwa jina lake Belteshaza. Na neno hilo lilikuwa kweli, na [lilihusu] vita vikubwa. Naye akalifahamu neno hilo, akawa na ufahamu wa maono hayo.
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa tatu wa utawala wa Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi, ujumbe ulijulishwa kwa Danieli, aliyekuwa amepewa jina Belteshaza. Ujumbe huo ulikuwa wa kweli, nao ulihusu vita vikubwa. Aliuelewa ujumbe huo; alipewa ufahamu katika maono.
sw.R: Katika mwaka wa tatu wa Koreshi kuwa mfalme wa Uajemi, ujumbe ulifunuliwa kwa Danieli, ambaye pia aliitwa Belteshaza. Ujumbe huo ulikuwa wa kweli. Ulihusu vita vikubwa. Danieli aliuelewa ujumbe huo. Alielewa maana ya maono hayo.

vi.L: Vào năm thứ ba của Si-ru vua Ba Tư, một lời đã được tỏ ra cho Đa-ni-ên, người được gọi tên là Bên-tơ-xát-sa. Và lời ấy là thật, và [nói về] một cuộc chiến lớn. Và ông hiểu lời ấy và có sự hiểu biết về khải tượng.
vi.B: Vào năm thứ ba triều vua Si-ru nước Ba Tư, một sứ điệp được tỏ cho Đa-ni-ên, người cũng được đặt tên là Bên-tơ-xát-sa. Sứ điệp ấy là thật, và nói về một cuộc chiến lớn. Ông hiểu sứ điệp ấy; ông được ban cho sự hiểu biết trong khải tượng.
vi.R: Vào năm thứ ba Si-ru làm vua Ba Tư, có một sứ điệp được bày tỏ cho Đa-ni-ên, người cũng được gọi là Bên-tơ-xát-sa. Sứ điệp ấy là thật. Nó nói về một cuộc chiến lớn. Đa-ni-ên hiểu sứ điệp ấy. Ông hiểu ý nghĩa của khải tượng.

decisions.choice: the third year of Cyrus: about 536 BC, the last date in the book
decisions.reason: Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BC, and his first year over it was counted from 538 (Ezra 1:1). His third year is about 536 BC. Daniel had served from the first year of Nebuchadnezzar to the first year of Cyrus (1:21); this is his last vision, and the longest. Chapters 10-12 are one vision: this chapter introduces it, 11:2-12:4 gives the message, and 12:5-13 ends it.

decisions.choice: Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar
decisions.reason: Belteshazzar is the Babylonian name given to Daniel at the court (1:7). Here, in the time of the Persians, the narrator reminds the reader of it. The verse speaks of Daniel in the third person; from verse 2 he tells the vision himself.

decisions.choice: a great conflict: a great war, or great hardship
decisions.reason: The word is the one for an army or warfare, and so for hard service (Isaiah 40:2; Job 7:1). The message concerns a great conflict: the wars of chapter 11 and the struggle in heaven of 10:13, 20-21, or the hardship they bring.

decisions.choice: in the third year of the reign of Cyrus (B); in Cyrus's third year as king (R)
decisions.reason: The date follows the wording set for dated headings in Jeremiah. Readable adds "also" for the second name.

decisions.choice: "Daniel, dont le nom était Beltshatsar" (L); names as the term sheet gives them (Cyrus, Beltshatsar, Michel, la Perse, la Grèce), and chapters 10-12 told in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable, as chapters 8-9
decisions.reason: "Beltshatsar" is the term sheet's form for Daniel's Babylonian name. Chapters 10-12 are Daniel's last vision, told as chapters 8-9; the angel's long speech (10:11-12:4) is speech, in the present, future and passé composé.

decisions.choice: "Ciro, rey de Persia"; "Beltsasar"
decisions.reason: The published form of Cyrus (2 Chronicles 36:22); Daniel's court name as in 1:7

decisions.choice: "Koreshi mfalme wa Uajemi"; "Belteshaza"
decisions.reason: The published forms of Ezra 1:1 and Daniel 1:7; the verse keeps the name Belteshazzar as its Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "Si-ru vua Ba Tư"; "Bên-tơ-xát-sa"; Daniel as "ông" in the third person
decisions.reason: The published forms (2 Chronicles 36:22; Daniel 1:7). Where the narrative speaks of Daniel in the third person, as here, he is "ông"; from verse 2 he says "tôi" again.

records.literal_gloss: In the days those I, Daniel, was mourning three sevens of days.

en.L: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks of days.
en.B: At that time I, Daniel, had been mourning for three whole weeks.
en.R: At that time I, Daniel, had been very sad for three weeks.

fr.L: En ces jours-là, moi, Daniel, j’étais en deuil [pendant] trois semaines de jours.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, moi, Daniel, j’étais en deuil depuis trois semaines entières.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, moi, Daniel, j’étais très triste depuis trois semaines.

es.L: En aquellos días yo, Daniel, estuve de luto tres semanas de días.
es.B: En aquel tiempo yo, Daniel, había estado de luto durante tres semanas completas.
es.R: En aquel tiempo yo, Daniel, había estado muy triste durante tres semanas.

sw.L: Katika siku hizo mimi Danieli nilikuwa nikiomboleza kwa majuma matatu ya siku.
sw.B: Wakati huo mimi Danieli nilikuwa nikiomboleza kwa majuma matatu kamili.
sw.R: Wakati huo mimi Danieli nilikuwa na huzuni nyingi kwa wiki tatu.

vi.L: Trong những ngày ấy, tôi, Đa-ni-ên, đã than khóc suốt ba tuần lễ trọn.
vi.B: Vào lúc ấy, tôi, Đa-ni-ên, đã sầu khổ suốt ba tuần lễ trọn.
vi.R: Lúc ấy, tôi, Đa-ni-ên, đã rất buồn rầu suốt ba tuần lễ.

decisions.choice: three weeks of days: three full weeks
decisions.reason: The word for "weeks" is the word "sevens" of 9:24-27. Here "of days" is added to make plain that these are weeks of days, perhaps to set them apart from the sevens of chapter 9.

decisions.choice: mourning: fasting and sorrow, perhaps for the state of the returned exiles
decisions.reason: Daniel does not say why he mourned. The return under Cyrus had begun (Ezra 1-3), but in about 536 BC the rebuilding of the temple met opposition and stopped (Ezra 4:4-5, 24). His mourning is a time of prayer and humbling himself (verse 12).

decisions.choice: weeks (all levels)
decisions.reason: Here the unit is stated ("of days"), so every level says "weeks"; in 9:24-27, where no unit is given, the word is "sevens".

decisions.choice: "trois semaines" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew adds "of days" to the sevens, so ordinary weeks are meant; French says "semaines", as the English "weeks", and keeps "septaines" for the unnamed sevens of 9:24-27.

decisions.choice: "semanas" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the sevens are "of days", so "semanas" is plain, as the English "weeks"; it is kept apart from the "sietes" of 9:24–27

decisions.choice: "majuma matatu" (L, B); "wiki tatu" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew adds "of days", and the English says "weeks" at every level, so Swahili uses the ordinary word for weeks; "majuma" is avoided only for the unit-less "sevens" of 9:24-27.

decisions.choice: "ba tuần lễ" for "three sevens of days"
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew adds "days" to the sevens, so the ordinary word for a week is right; in 9:24-27, where no unit is given, the sevens stay "bộ bảy".

source.text: לֶ֣חֶם חֲמֻד֞וֹת לֹ֣א אָכַ֗לְתִּי וּבָשָׂ֥ר וָיַ֛יִן לֹא־בָ֥א אֶל־פִּ֖י וְס֣וֹךְ לֹא־סָ֑כְתִּי עַד־מְלֹ֕את שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת שָׁבֻעִ֖ים יָמִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Food of desirablenesses not I ate, and meat and wine not came into my mouth, and anointing not I anointed myself, until were completed three sevens of days.

en.L: I ate no pleasant food, and no meat or wine came into my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all, until the three weeks of days were completed.
en.B: I ate no fine food; no meat or wine passed my lips, and I did not put any oil on myself until the three weeks were over.
en.R: I did not eat any rich food. I did not eat any meat or drink any wine. I did not put any lotion on my skin until those three weeks were over.

fr.L: Je ne mangeai aucun mets désirable, et ni viande ni vin n’entrèrent dans ma bouche, et je ne m’oignis pas du tout, jusqu’à ce que fussent accomplies les trois semaines de jours.
fr.B: Je ne mangeai aucun mets délicat, ni viande ni vin n’entrèrent dans ma bouche, et je ne me parfumai pas d’huile, jusqu’à ce que les trois semaines soient passées.
fr.R: Je n’ai mangé aucun bon plat. Je n’ai mangé ni viande ni bu de vin. Je ne me suis pas mis de crème sur la peau avant la fin de ces trois semaines.

es.L: No comí manjar delicado, ni entró en mi boca carne ni vino, ni me ungí en absoluto, hasta que se cumplieron las tres semanas de días.
es.B: No comí alimentos refinados; no probé carne ni vino, y no me puse aceite hasta que pasaron las tres semanas.
es.R: No comí ninguna comida sabrosa. No comí carne ni bebí vino. No me puse ninguna loción en la piel hasta que pasaron esas tres semanas.

sw.L: Sikula chakula kitamu, wala nyama wala divai haikuingia kinywani mwangu, wala sikujipaka mafuta hata kidogo, mpaka majuma matatu ya siku yalipotimia.
sw.B: Sikula chakula kizuri; nyama wala divai haikugusa midomo yangu, wala sikujipaka mafuta yoyote mpaka majuma hayo matatu yalipokwisha.
sw.R: Sikula chakula kitamu chochote. Sikula nyama wala kunywa divai. Sikujipaka mafuta yoyote mwilini mpaka wiki hizo tatu zilipokwisha.

vi.L: Tôi không ăn thức ăn ngon, và thịt và rượu không vào miệng tôi, và tôi hoàn toàn không xức dầu cho mình, cho đến khi ba tuần lễ trọn đã mãn.
vi.B: Tôi không ăn món ngon, không để thịt hay rượu vào miệng, cũng không thoa dầu lên mình cho đến khi hết ba tuần lễ ấy.
vi.R: Tôi không ăn những món ngon. Tôi không ăn thịt cũng không uống rượu. Tôi không thoa dầu thơm lên da cho đến khi ba tuần lễ ấy qua đi.

decisions.choice: anoint myself: rub oil on the skin
decisions.reason: Olive oil was rubbed on the skin and hair to refresh it and to keep it from drying in the heat (Ruth 3:3; 2 Samuel 14:2; Matthew 6:17). Leaving it off was a sign of mourning.

decisions.choice: pleasant food: rich, choice food
decisions.reason: "Food of desires" is the good food one would enjoy, as against plain food. Daniel's fast was partial, as his diet of vegetables was in 1:12.

decisions.choice: put any oil on myself (B); put any lotion on my skin (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "anoint"; Balanced and Readable say what it was (m1), since "anoint" suggests a religious rite to a modern reader.

decisions.choice: "je ne me parfumai pas d'huile" (B), "je ne me suis pas mis de crème sur la peau" (R)
alternatives: "je ne m'oignis pas" at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb "oindre"; Balanced and Readable say what the custom was, rubbing oil on the skin, as the English does.

source.text: וּבְי֛וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וַאֲנִ֗י הָיִ֛יתִי עַ֣ל יַ֧ד הַנָּהָ֛ר הַגָּד֖וֹל ה֥וּא חִדָּֽקֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And on day twenty and four of the month the first, and I was on [the] side of the river the great, it [is] Hiddekel,

en.L: And on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, while I was by the side of the great river, that is, the Tigris,
en.B: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, the Tigris.
en.R: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing beside the great Tigris River.

fr.L: Et le vingt-quatrième jour du premier mois, moi, j’étais au bord du grand fleuve, c’[est] le Tigre,
fr.B: Le vingt-quatrième jour du premier mois, j’étais au bord du grand fleuve, le Tigre.
fr.R: Le vingt-quatrième jour du premier mois, je me trouvais au bord du grand fleuve Tigre.

es.L: Y el día veinticuatro del mes primero, estando yo a la orilla del gran río, que es el Tigris,
es.B: El día veinticuatro del primer mes, yo estaba a la orilla del gran río, el Tigris.
es.R: El día veinticuatro del primer mes, yo estaba de pie a la orilla del gran río Tigris.

sw.L: Na siku ya ishirini na nne ya mwezi wa kwanza, nilipokuwa kando ya mto ule mkubwa, yaani, Tigri,
sw.B: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya mwezi wa kwanza, nilikuwa kando ya mto mkubwa, Tigri.
sw.R: Siku ya ishirini na nne ya mwezi wa kwanza, nilikuwa nimesimama kando ya mto mkubwa wa Tigri.

vi.L: Và vào ngày hai mươi bốn tháng thứ nhất, khi tôi đang ở bên bờ con sông lớn, tức là sông Ti-gơ-rơ,
vi.B: Vào ngày hai mươi bốn tháng thứ nhất, tôi đang ở bên bờ con sông lớn là sông Ti-gơ-rơ.
vi.R: Vào ngày hai mươi bốn tháng thứ nhất, tôi đang đứng bên bờ con sông lớn Ti-gơ-rơ.

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth day of the first month: in the spring, just after Passover
decisions.reason: The first month, Nisan, is in March-April. Passover fell on the fourteenth day, with the Festival of Unleavened Bread from the fifteenth to the twenty-first (Leviticus 23:5-6). Daniel's three weeks of fasting would have run through the festival days.

decisions.choice: the great river, the Tigris: the Hebrew name is Hiddekel
decisions.reason: Hiddekel is the Hebrew name of the Tigris, one of the four rivers of Eden (Genesis 2:14). Elsewhere "the great river" is the Euphrates (Genesis 15:18), but here it is said to be the Tigris, which flows past Babylon to the east. Some ancient translations read the Euphrates here.

decisions.choice: the Tigris (all levels)
decisions.reason: Every level uses the familiar name for Hiddekel (m2). Literal ends with a comma, since the sentence runs into verse 5.

decisions.choice: "el Tigris" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English; the Hebrew name Hiddekel is in the meaning decision

decisions.choice: "Tigri" at every level
decisions.reason: The English says Tigris at every level, and "Tigri" is the published name for the river in Genesis 2:14.

decisions.choice: "sông Ti-gơ-rơ" for Hiddekel at every level
decisions.reason: The published name of the same river in Genesis 2:14, as the English gives "the Tigris" at every level.

records.literal_gloss: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man, one, clothed [in] linen, and his loins girded with gold of Uphaz.

en.L: I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man clothed in linen, and his waist was girded with gold of Uphaz.
en.B: I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen, wearing around his waist a belt of fine gold from Uphaz.
en.R: I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen clothes. He had a belt of pure gold around his waist.

fr.L: et je levai les yeux et je vis, et voici, un homme vêtu de lin, et ses reins ceints d’or d’Ouphaz.
fr.B: Je levai les yeux et je vis un homme vêtu de lin, qui portait autour de la taille une ceinture d’or pur d’Ouphaz.
fr.R: J’ai levé les yeux et j’ai vu un homme habillé de vêtements de lin. Il avait une ceinture d’or pur autour de la taille.

es.L: Y alcé mis ojos y miré, y he aquí un hombre vestido de lino, y sus lomos ceñidos con oro de Ufaz.
es.B: Levanté la vista y vi a un hombre vestido de lino, con un cinturón de oro fino de Ufaz en la cintura.
es.R: Miré y vi a un hombre vestido con ropa de lino. Tenía un cinturón de oro puro en la cintura.

sw.L: nikainua macho yangu, nikaona, na tazama, mtu mmoja aliyevaa kitani, na kiuno chake kimefungwa dhahabu ya Ufazi.
sw.B: Nikainua macho, nikaona mtu aliyevaa nguo za kitani, naye amejifunga kiunoni mshipi wa dhahabu safi ya Ufazi.
sw.R: Nilitazama juu nikaona mtu aliyevaa nguo za kitani. Alikuwa amejifunga mshipi wa dhahabu safi kiunoni.

vi.L: Tôi ngước mắt lên và nhìn, và kìa, một người mặc vải gai, và lưng người thắt [đai] vàng U-pha.
vi.B: Tôi ngước mắt lên và thấy một người mặc áo vải gai, lưng thắt đai bằng vàng ròng U-pha.
vi.R: Tôi nhìn lên và thấy một người mặc quần áo bằng vải gai. Lưng người ấy thắt một cái đai bằng vàng ròng.

decisions.choice: a man clothed in linen: a heavenly being
decisions.reason: The man clothed in linen is like the one in Ezekiel's vision who marks the faithful (Ezekiel 9:2-3; 10:2) and like the angel of 12:6-7. Linen is the dress of priests (Leviticus 16:4) and of heavenly beings. He is not named. Most read him as an angel, perhaps Gabriel, who goes on to speak in verses 11-14 and needs Michael's help (verse 13); some read the glorious figure of verses 5-6 as a different and greater being than the one who speaks, and Christian readers have often seen a likeness to the risen Christ of Revelation 1:13-15. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: gold of Uphaz: fine gold
decisions.reason: Uphaz is named again only in Jeremiah 10:9 as a source of gold. Its place is unknown; some take it as a form of Ophir, famous for its gold (1 Kings 9:28).

decisions.choice: a man; his (no deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: The figure is described as a man, as Gabriel is in 9:21, and the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, since he is a heavenly messenger (m1). Readable says "pure gold" for gold of Uphaz.

decisions.choice: "un homme", "ses", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the English: the meaning decision leaves open who the heavenly being is, and the term sheet gives spans only to God and the Ancient of Days.

decisions.choice: "Ufaz" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The form published in Jeremiah 10:9; R gives the sense, as the English R does. The man takes no deity_pronoun span

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on the man in linen; "Ufazi" as Jeremiah 10:9
decisions.reason: As the English and the term sheet: the man in linen is a heavenly messenger, not God, so his pronouns stay plain throughout chapters 10-12.

decisions.choice: "một người mặc vải gai", with "người" and no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the man clothed in linen of Ezekiel 9:2. The meaning decision reads him as a heavenly being, and the English gives him no deity pronoun, so Vietnamese uses the plain "người" for him. "U-pha" is the published form of Jeremiah 10:9.

source.text: וּגְוִיָּת֣וֹ כְתַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ וּפָנָ֞יו כְּמַרְאֵ֤ה בָרָק֙ וְעֵינָיו֙ כְּלַפִּ֣ידֵי אֵ֔שׁ וּזְרֹֽעֹתָיו֙ וּמַרְגְּלֹתָ֔יו כְּעֵ֖ין נְחֹ֣שֶׁת קָלָ֑ל וְק֥וֹל דְּבָרָ֖יו כְּק֥וֹל הָמֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And his body [was] like chrysolite, and his face like [the] appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and his feet like [the] gleam of bronze burnished, and the sound of his words like [the] sound of a multitude.

en.L: And his body was like chrysolite, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and his feet like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
en.B: His body shone like chrysolite, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, and his arms and legs gleamed like polished bronze. His voice sounded like the noise of a great crowd.
en.R: His body shone like a precious stone. His face was as bright as lightning, and his eyes were like flaming torches. His arms and legs shone like polished bronze. When he spoke, his voice sounded like a huge crowd of people.

fr.L: Et son corps [était] comme de la chrysolithe, et son visage comme l’aspect de l’éclair, et ses yeux comme des torches de feu, et ses bras et ses pieds comme l’éclat du bronze poli, et le son de ses paroles comme le bruit d’une multitude.
fr.B: Son corps brillait comme la chrysolithe, son visage comme l’éclair, ses yeux comme des torches enflammées, et ses bras et ses jambes étincelaient comme du bronze poli. Sa voix résonnait comme le bruit d’une grande foule.
fr.R: Son corps brillait comme une pierre précieuse. Son visage était aussi lumineux qu’un éclair, et ses yeux étaient comme des torches enflammées. Ses bras et ses jambes brillaient comme du bronze poli. Quand il parlait, sa voix ressemblait au bruit d’une foule immense.

es.L: Y su cuerpo [era] como crisólito, y su rostro como el aspecto del relámpago, y sus ojos como antorchas de fuego, y sus brazos y sus pies como el brillo del bronce bruñido, y el sonido de sus palabras como el sonido de una multitud.
es.B: Su cuerpo brillaba como el crisólito, su rostro como el relámpago, sus ojos como antorchas encendidas, y sus brazos y sus piernas relucían como bronce pulido. Su voz sonaba como el ruido de una gran multitud.
es.R: Su cuerpo brillaba como una piedra preciosa. Su rostro era tan brillante como un relámpago, y sus ojos eran como antorchas encendidas. Sus brazos y sus piernas brillaban como bronce pulido. Cuando hablaba, su voz sonaba como una enorme multitud de gente.

sw.L: Na mwili wake ulikuwa kama krisolito, na uso wake kama sura ya umeme, na macho yake kama mienge ya moto, na mikono yake na miguu yake kama mng'ao wa shaba iliyosuguliwa, na sauti ya maneno yake kama sauti ya umati.
sw.B: Mwili wake uling'aa kama krisolito, uso wake kama umeme, macho yake kama mienge inayowaka, na mikono na miguu yake ilimeremeta kama shaba iliyosuguliwa. Sauti yake ilisikika kama kelele za umati mkubwa.
sw.R: Mwili wake uling'aa kama jiwe la thamani. Uso wake ulikuwa na mwanga kama umeme, na macho yake yalikuwa kama mienge inayowaka. Mikono na miguu yake ilimeremeta kama shaba iliyosuguliwa. Alipozungumza, sauti yake ilisikika kama kelele za kundi kubwa la watu.

vi.L: Và thân thể người như hoàng thạch, và mặt người như diện mạo của tia chớp, và mắt người như những ngọn đuốc lửa, và cánh tay cùng bàn chân người như ánh của đồng đánh bóng, và tiếng nói của người như tiếng của một đám đông.
vi.B: Thân thể người sáng như hoàng thạch, mặt như tia chớp, mắt như ngọn đuốc cháy, tay và chân sáng loáng như đồng đánh bóng. Tiếng nói của người như tiếng ồn ào của một đám đông lớn.
vi.R: Thân thể người sáng lấp lánh như một loại đá quý. Mặt người sáng chói như tia chớp, và mắt người như những ngọn đuốc đang cháy. Tay và chân người sáng loáng như đồng được đánh bóng. Khi người nói, tiếng người vang như tiếng của một đám đông rất lớn.

decisions.choice: chrysolite: a gold-colored precious stone
decisions.reason: The stone is named after Tarshish. It is one of the stones of the high priest's breastplate (Exodus 28:20) and of the wheels in Ezekiel's vision (Ezekiel 1:16; 10:9). Which stone it is is not certain: chrysolite, beryl or topaz have been suggested.

decisions.choice: eyes like torches, limbs like bronze, a voice like a multitude: Ezekiel 1 and Revelation 1
decisions.reason: The description recalls the living creatures and the glory of Ezekiel 1:7, 13-14, 24, and is echoed in the risen Jesus of Revelation 1:14-15, whose eyes are "like a flame of fire" and feet "like burnished bronze".

decisions.choice: legs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for feet is used of the legs as well (as in Ezekiel 1:7); Balanced and Readable say "legs", the limb that would gleam with the arms. Readable says "a precious stone" for chrysolite (m1).

decisions.choice: "krisolito" (L, B); "jiwe la thamani" (R)
decisions.reason: "Krisolito" is the published stone of Exodus 28:20, as the term sheet sets for Ezekiel 1:16; Readable says what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "hoàng thạch" (L, B); "một loại đá quý" (R)
decisions.reason: The published word for tarshish in Exodus 28:20 and Ezekiel 1:16; Readable says only that it is a precious stone, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְרָאִיתִי֩ אֲנִ֨י דָנִיֵּ֤אל לְבַדִּי֙ אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֔ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹ֥א רָא֖וּ אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֑ה אֲבָ֗ל חֲרָדָ֤ה גְדֹלָה֙ נָפְלָ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַֽיִּבְרְח֖וּ בְּהֵחָבֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And I saw, I, Daniel, I alone, the vision, and the men who were with me not saw the vision, but trembling great fell on them, and they fled in hiding themselves.

en.L: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision; but a great trembling fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.
en.B: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see it, but such terror came over them that they ran away and hid.
en.R: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see it. But they were so frightened that they ran away and hid.

fr.L: Et moi, Daniel, je vis seul la vision, et les hommes qui étaient avec moi ne virent pas la vision ; mais un grand tremblement tomba sur eux, et ils s’enfuirent pour se cacher.
fr.B: Moi, Daniel, je fus le seul à voir la vision. Les hommes qui étaient avec moi ne la virent pas, mais une telle terreur les saisit qu’ils s’enfuirent et se cachèrent.
fr.R: Moi, Daniel, j’ai été le seul à voir la vision. Les hommes qui étaient avec moi ne l’ont pas vue. Mais ils ont eu tellement peur qu’ils se sont enfuis et se sont cachés.

es.L: Y solo yo, Daniel, vi la visión, y los hombres que estaban conmigo no vieron la visión; pero cayó sobre ellos un gran temblor, y huyeron para esconderse.
es.B: Solo yo, Daniel, vi la visión. Los hombres que estaban conmigo no la vieron, pero les entró tanto terror que huyeron y se escondieron.
es.R: Yo, Daniel, fui el único que vio la visión. Los hombres que estaban conmigo no la vieron. Pero tuvieron tanto miedo que huyeron y se escondieron.

sw.L: Na mimi Danieli peke yangu niliyaona maono hayo, na watu waliokuwa pamoja nami hawakuyaona maono hayo; lakini tetemeko kubwa likawaangukia, wakakimbia kujificha.
sw.B: Mimi Danieli ndiye peke yangu niliyeyaona maono hayo. Watu waliokuwa pamoja nami hawakuyaona, lakini hofu kuu iliwashika hata wakakimbia na kujificha.
sw.R: Mimi Danieli ndiye peke yangu niliyeyaona maono hayo. Watu waliokuwa pamoja nami hawakuyaona. Lakini waliogopa sana, wakakimbia na kujificha.

vi.L: Và chỉ một mình tôi, Đa-ni-ên, thấy khải tượng, còn những người ở với tôi không thấy khải tượng; nhưng một sự run sợ lớn giáng trên họ, và họ chạy trốn để ẩn mình.
vi.B: Chỉ một mình tôi, Đa-ni-ên, thấy khải tượng. Những người ở với tôi không thấy, nhưng họ kinh hãi đến nỗi bỏ chạy và ẩn trốn.
vi.R: Chỉ một mình tôi, Đa-ni-ên, thấy khải tượng ấy. Những người ở với tôi không thấy. Nhưng họ sợ hãi đến nỗi bỏ chạy đi trốn.

decisions.choice: the men with me did not see the vision: compare Acts 9:7
decisions.reason: When the risen Jesus appeared to Paul, the men with him heard a sound but saw no one (Acts 9:7; 22:9). Here Daniel's companions see nothing but feel the presence and flee.

decisions.choice: such terror came over them (B); they were so frightened (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "a great trembling fell upon them"; Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

source.text: וַאֲנִי֙ נִשְׁאַ֣רְתִּי לְבַדִּ֔י וָֽאֶרְאֶ֗ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹ֥א נִשְׁאַר־בִּ֖י כֹּ֑ח וְהוֹדִ֗י נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ עָלַי֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית וְלֹ֥א עָצַ֖רְתִּי כֹּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I was left, I alone, and I saw the vision the great this, and not remained in me strength, and my vigor was changed on me to ruin, and not I retained strength.

en.L: So I was left alone and saw this great vision, and no strength remained in me; my vigor was turned to ruin in me, and I retained no strength.
en.B: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision. I had no strength left; my face turned deathly pale, and I was helpless.
en.R: So I was left alone, looking at this great vision. I had no strength left. My face turned very pale, and I felt completely weak.

fr.L: Et moi, je restai seul, et je vis cette grande vision, et il ne resta pas de force en moi ; et mon éclat se changea sur moi en ruine, et je ne gardai aucune force.
fr.B: Je restai donc seul à contempler cette grande vision. Il ne me restait plus de force ; mon visage devint d’une pâleur mortelle, et j’étais sans force.
fr.R: Je suis donc resté seul à regarder cette grande vision. Je n’avais plus de force. Mon visage est devenu tout pâle, et je me sentais complètement faible.

es.L: Quedé, pues, yo solo, y vi esta gran visión, y no quedó en mí fuerza; mi vigor se me cambió en ruina, y no retuve fuerza alguna.
es.B: Así que me quedé solo, contemplando esta gran visión. Me quedé sin fuerzas; mi rostro se puso pálido como el de un muerto, y no podía hacer nada.
es.R: Así que me quedé solo, mirando esta gran visión. Ya no me quedaban fuerzas. Mi cara se puso muy pálida y me sentí completamente débil.

sw.L: Basi nikabaki peke yangu, nikayaona maono haya makubwa, wala hazikubaki nguvu ndani yangu; uzuri wa sura yangu ukageuka ndani yangu kuwa uharibifu, wala sikuweza kubaki na nguvu.
sw.B: Basi nikabaki peke yangu, nikiyatazama maono haya makubwa. Sikubaki na nguvu yoyote; uso wangu ukageuka kuwa mweupe kama wa mfu, nami nikawa sina uwezo.
sw.R: Basi nikabaki peke yangu, nikiyatazama maono haya makubwa. Sikuwa na nguvu tena. Uso wangu ukapauka sana, nami nikajisikia dhaifu kabisa.

vi.L: Vậy tôi bị để lại một mình và thấy khải tượng lớn này, và không còn sức lực trong tôi; vẻ tươi tắn của tôi đổi thành tàn tạ, và tôi không còn giữ được sức lực nào.
vi.B: Vậy tôi ở lại một mình, nhìn khải tượng lớn lao này. Tôi không còn chút sức lực nào; mặt tôi tái mét như người chết, và tôi hoàn toàn kiệt sức.
vi.R: Vậy tôi ở lại một mình, nhìn khải tượng lớn lao này. Tôi không còn chút sức lực nào. Mặt tôi tái nhợt, và tôi thấy mình yếu đuối hoàn toàn.

decisions.choice: my vigor was turned to ruin: my healthy look was gone, I grew deathly pale
decisions.reason: The word for vigor means splendor or a healthy look (Isaiah 53:2, "majesty"). It was "turned to destruction": the color drained from his face, as in 7:28.

decisions.choice: my face turned deathly pale (B); my face turned very pale (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

source.text: וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע אֶת־ק֣וֹל דְּבָרָ֑יו וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל דְּבָרָ֔יו וַאֲנִ֗י הָיִ֛יתִי נִרְדָּ֥ם עַל־פָּנַ֖י וּפָנַ֥י אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I was dazed on my face, and my face to the ground.

en.L: Then I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I sank into a deep sleep on my face, my face to the ground.
en.B: Then I heard him speaking, and as I listened to the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep, face down, with my face to the ground.
en.R: Then I heard him speaking. As I listened to his voice, I fainted and lay with my face on the ground.

fr.L: Et j’entendis le son de ses paroles ; et quand j’entendis le son de ses paroles, je tombai dans un profond sommeil sur ma face, ma face contre terre.
fr.B: Puis je l’entendis parler, et en écoutant le son de ses paroles, je sombrai dans un profond sommeil, face contre terre.
fr.R: Puis je l’ai entendu parler. En écoutant sa voix, je me suis évanoui et je suis resté le visage contre le sol.

es.L: Entonces oí el sonido de sus palabras; y al oír el sonido de sus palabras, caí en un sueño profundo sobre mi rostro, con mi rostro en tierra.
es.B: Entonces lo oí hablar, y al escuchar el sonido de sus palabras, caí en un sueño profundo, boca abajo, con el rostro en tierra.
es.R: Entonces lo oí hablar. Al escuchar su voz, me desmayé y quedé tendido con la cara en el suelo.

sw.L: Kisha nikasikia sauti ya maneno yake; na niliposikia sauti ya maneno yake, nikawa katika usingizi mzito kifudifudi, uso wangu ukiwa chini.
sw.B: Kisha nikamsikia akisema, na nilipokuwa nikisikiliza sauti ya maneno yake, nilipatwa na usingizi mzito, nikiwa kifudifudi, uso wangu ukiwa ardhini.
sw.R: Kisha nikamsikia akisema. Nilipokuwa nikiisikiliza sauti yake, nilizimia, nikalala kifudifudi ardhini.

vi.L: Rồi tôi nghe tiếng lời người nói; và khi tôi nghe tiếng lời người nói, tôi ngủ mê, sấp mặt, mặt tôi xuống đất.
vi.B: Rồi tôi nghe người nói, và khi tôi lắng nghe tiếng của những lời ấy, tôi chìm vào giấc ngủ mê, nằm sấp, mặt úp xuống đất.
vi.R: Rồi tôi nghe người nói. Khi nghe tiếng người, tôi ngất đi và nằm úp mặt xuống đất.

decisions.choice: I fell into a deep sleep on my face: as in 8:18
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 8:18 when Gabriel spoke to Daniel. He was overcome and lost consciousness.

decisions.choice: I fainted (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:18, Readable says what the deep sleep was.

decisions.choice: "caí en un sueño profundo" (L, B); "me desmayé" (R)
decisions.reason: Worded as 8:18, which this verse recalls

source.text: וְהִנֵּה־יָ֖ד נָ֣גְעָה בִּ֑י וַתְּנִיעֵ֥נִי עַל־בִּרְכַּ֖י וְכַפּ֥וֹת יָדָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, a hand touched me, and it set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.

en.L: And look, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.
en.B: Then a hand touched me and raised me, trembling, onto my hands and knees.
en.R: Suddenly a hand touched me. It helped me get up on my hands and knees, though I was shaking.

fr.L: Et voici, une main me toucha et me fit [me] dresser, tremblant, sur mes genoux et sur les paumes de mes mains.
fr.B: Alors une main me toucha et me redressa, tout tremblant, sur les mains et les genoux.
fr.R: Tout à coup, une main m’a touché. Elle m’a aidé à me relever sur les mains et les genoux, mais je tremblais.

es.L: Y he aquí, una mano me tocó, y me hizo temblar sobre mis rodillas y sobre las palmas de mis manos.
es.B: Entonces una mano me tocó y me levantó, tembloroso, sobre las manos y las rodillas.
es.R: De pronto una mano me tocó. Me ayudó a levantarme sobre las manos y las rodillas, aunque yo temblaba.

sw.L: Na tazama, mkono ukanigusa, ukaniinua nikitetemeka juu ya magoti yangu na viganja vya mikono yangu.
sw.B: Kisha mkono ulinigusa, ukaniinua, nikitetemeka, nikasimama kwa magoti na mikono yangu.
sw.R: Ghafla mkono ulinigusa. Ulinisaidia kuinuka kwa mikono na magoti yangu, ingawa nilikuwa nikitetemeka.

vi.L: Và kìa, một bàn tay chạm vào tôi và làm cho tôi run rẩy chống trên đầu gối và lòng bàn tay.
vi.B: Rồi một bàn tay chạm vào tôi và đỡ tôi dậy, run rẩy chống tay và đầu gối.
vi.R: Thình lình có một bàn tay chạm vào tôi. Bàn tay ấy giúp tôi chống tay và đầu gối mà dậy, dù tôi vẫn còn run rẩy.

decisions.choice: set me trembling: shook me up, raised me trembling
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone shake, and here also to rouse him: the hand shakes Daniel awake and raises him onto his hands and knees, still trembling.

decisions.choice: set me, trembling, on my hands and knees (B); helped me get up ... though I was shaking (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep both parts of the verb's sense (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֡י דָּנִיֵּ֣אל אִישׁ־חֲ֠מֻדוֹת הָבֵ֨ן בַּדְּבָרִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר֩ אָנֹכִ֨י דֹבֵ֤ר אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ וַעֲמֹ֣ד עַל־עָמְדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה שֻׁלַּ֣חְתִּי אֵלֶ֑יךָ וּבְדַבְּר֥וֹ עִמִּ֛י אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה עָמַ֥דְתִּי מַרְעִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me: Daniel, man of preciousnesses, understand the words which I am speaking to you, and stand on your place, for now I have been sent to you. And when he spoke with me this word, I stood up trembling.

en.L: And he said to me, "Daniel, man greatly loved, understand the words that I am speaking to you, and stand upright, for now I have been sent to you." And when he spoke this word to me, I stood up trembling.
en.B: He said to me, "Daniel, you are greatly loved. Pay attention to the words I am about to speak to you, and stand up, for I have been sent to you." When he said this to me, I stood up, trembling.
en.R: He said to me, "Daniel, God loves you very much. Listen carefully to what I am going to tell you. Stand up, because I have been sent to you." When he said this to me, I stood up. I was still shaking.

fr.L: Et il me dit : « Daniel, homme bien-aimé, comprends les paroles que je te dis, et tiens-toi debout à ta place, car maintenant j’ai été envoyé vers toi. » Et quand il m’eut dit cette parole, je me tins debout en tremblant.
fr.B: Il me dit : « Daniel, toi qui es tant aimé, sois attentif aux paroles que je vais te dire, et lève-toi, car j’ai été envoyé vers toi. » Quand il m’eut dit cela, je me levai en tremblant.
fr.R: Il m’a dit : « Daniel, Dieu t’aime beaucoup. Écoute bien ce que je vais te dire. Lève-toi, car j’ai été envoyé vers toi. » Quand il m’a dit cela, je me suis levé. Je tremblais encore.

es.L: Y me dijo: «Daniel, hombre muy amado, entiende las palabras que te hablo, y ponte en pie en tu lugar, porque ahora he sido enviado a ti». Y mientras me decía esta palabra, me puse en pie temblando.
es.B: Me dijo: «Daniel, hombre muy amado, presta atención a las palabras que voy a decirte y ponte de pie, porque he sido enviado a ti». Cuando me dijo esto, me puse de pie, temblando.
es.R: Me dijo: «Daniel, Dios te ama mucho. Escucha con atención lo que te voy a decir. Ponte de pie, porque he sido enviado a ti». Cuando me dijo esto, me puse de pie. Todavía estaba temblando.

sw.B: Akaniambia, "Danieli, unapendwa sana. Yazingatie maneno ninayokaribia kukuambia, usimame, kwa sababu nimetumwa kwako." Aliponiambia hayo, nikasimama, nikitetemeka.
sw.R: Akaniambia, "Danieli, Mungu anakupenda sana. Sikiliza kwa makini nitakayokuambia. Simama, kwa sababu nimetumwa kwako." Aliponiambia hayo, nilisimama. Bado nilikuwa nikitetemeka.

vi.R: Người nói với tôi: "Đa-ni-ên, Đức Chúa Trời rất yêu quý ông. Hãy lắng nghe kỹ điều tôi sắp nói với ông. Hãy đứng dậy, vì tôi đã được sai đến với ông." Khi người nói điều ấy với tôi, tôi đứng dậy. Tôi vẫn còn run rẩy.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me: Do not fear, Daniel, for from the day the first that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.

en.L: And he said to me, "Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you gave your heart to understanding and to humbling yourself before your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words.

fr.L: Et il me dit : « Ne crains pas, Daniel, car depuis le premier jour où tu as appliqué ton cœur à comprendre et à t’humilier devant ton Dieu, tes paroles ont été entendues, et je suis venu à cause de tes paroles.
fr.B: Puis il me dit : « N’aie pas peur, Daniel. Dès le premier jour où tu as décidé de comprendre et de t’humilier devant ton Dieu, tes paroles ont été entendues, et c’est pour y répondre que je suis venu.
fr.R: Puis il m’a dit : « N’aie pas peur, Daniel. Dès le premier jour où tu as décidé de comprendre et de t’humilier devant ton Dieu, Dieu a entendu tes prières. Je suis venu à cause de tes prières.

es.L: Y me dijo: «No temas, Daniel, porque desde el primer día que dispusiste tu corazón a entender y a humillarte delante de tu Dios, fueron oídas tus palabras, y yo he venido a causa de tus palabras.

es.R: Entonces me dijo: «No tengas miedo, Daniel. Desde el primer día en que decidiste entender y humillarte delante de tu Dios, Dios escuchó tus oraciones. He venido por causa de tus oraciones.

sw.L: Naye akaniambia, "Usiogope, Danieli, kwa maana tangu siku ya kwanza ulipouelekeza moyo wako kufahamu na kujinyenyekeza mbele ya Mungu wako, maneno yako yamesikiwa, nami nimekuja kwa sababu ya maneno yako.

vi.R: Rồi người nói với tôi: "Đa-ni-ên, đừng sợ. Từ ngày đầu tiên ông quyết định tìm hiểu và hạ mình trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời của ông, Đức Chúa Trời đã nghe lời cầu nguyện của ông. Tôi đến là vì lời cầu nguyện của ông.

en.L: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia was standing against me for twenty-one days; and look, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my help, since I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
en.B: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood in my way for twenty-one days, until Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my aid, because I had been left there alone with the kings of Persia.
en.R: But the ruling angel of the kingdom of Persia stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the most important ruling angels, came to help me. I had been left there alone with the kings of Persia.

fr.R: Mais l’ange qui gouverne le royaume de Perse s’est opposé à moi pendant vingt et un jours. Alors Michel, l’un des anges les plus importants, est venu m’aider. J’étais resté là, seul face aux rois de Perse.

es.L: Pero el príncipe del reino de Persia se me opuso durante veintiún días; y he aquí, Miguel, uno de los principales príncipes, vino a ayudarme, porque yo había quedado allí junto a los reyes de Persia.

es.R: Pero el ángel gobernante del reino de Persia se me opuso durante veintiún días. Entonces Miguel, uno de los ángeles gobernantes más importantes, vino a ayudarme. Yo me había quedado allí solo con los reyes de Persia.

vi.L: Nhưng thủ lĩnh của vương quốc Ba Tư đã đứng chống lại tôi hai mươi mốt ngày; và kìa, Mi-ca-ên, một trong các thủ lĩnh hàng đầu, đã đến giúp tôi, vì tôi đã bị để lại ở đó với các vua Ba Tư.
vi.B: Nhưng thủ lĩnh của vương quốc Ba Tư đã cản đường tôi suốt hai mươi mốt ngày, cho đến khi Mi-ca-ên, một trong các thủ lĩnh hàng đầu, đến giúp tôi, vì tôi đã bị bỏ lại một mình ở đó với các vua Ba Tư.
vi.R: Nhưng thiên sứ cai quản vương quốc Ba Tư đã chống lại tôi suốt hai mươi mốt ngày. Rồi Mi-ca-ên, một trong những thiên sứ cai quản quan trọng nhất, đến giúp tôi. Tôi đã bị bỏ lại một mình ở đó với các vua Ba Tư.

decisions.choice: the prince of the kingdom of Persia: a heavenly power set over Persia
decisions.reason: This prince opposes God's messenger for three weeks, the length of Daniel's fast (verse 2), and Michael, a heavenly prince, comes to help. So this prince is usually understood as a spiritual being, an angelic power linked with the kingdom of Persia, as "the prince of Greece" is with Greece (verse 20). The idea that the nations have heavenly rulers is found also in Deuteronomy 32:8 in some ancient witnesses, and in Isaiah 24:21. Some read the prince as the human king of Persia, but the battle with Michael makes that hard. The text gives no more detail.

decisions.choice: Michael, one of the chief princes: the angel who stands for Israel
decisions.reason: Michael's name means "Who is like God?". In Daniel he is "your prince" (verse 21) and "the great prince who stands over your people" (12:1). Jude 9 calls him the archangel, and in Revelation 12:7 he and his angels fight the dragon.

decisions.choice: I had been left there with the kings of Persia
alternatives: I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of Persia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "I was left there with the kings of Persia", meaning the messenger was held back alone there until Michael came. Some ancient translations read "I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of Persia", which says that Michael took over the struggle. The sense of the passage is the same.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruling angel (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruling angel" at Readable for the word sar where it names an angel. Readable says what kind of prince is meant, since a reader would otherwise think of a human prince; that the princes of Persia and Greece are angels is the usual reading but not certain (see the meaning decision at 10:13).

decisions.choice: "le prince" (L, B), "l'ange qui gouverne", "l'un des anges les plus importants" (R) for sar of an angel, for chapters 10-12; "Michel" as Jude 9 and Revelation 12:7
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets: Readable says that a heavenly power is meant, as the English "ruling angel" does.

decisions.choice: "príncipe" (L, B); "ángel gobernante" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for sar used of an angel (10:13, 20–21; 12:1), uncertain at R as in the English

decisions.choice: "Miguel, uno de los principales príncipes"
decisions.reason: Michael's published name (Jude 9; Revelation 12:7) and the settled wording of his title

decisions.choice: "mkuu" (L, B) for the sar of an angel, so Michael is "mmoja wa wakuu walio wakuu"; "malaika mtawala" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's one word for human and heavenly princes, and Readable names the ruling angel as the English Readable does. "Malaika mkuu" is avoided because it is the published title "archangel" of Jude 9.

decisions.choice: "Mikaeli"
decisions.reason: The published form of Jude 9 and Revelation 12:7.

decisions.choice: "thủ lĩnh" (L, B); "thiên sứ cai quản" (R) for sar as an angel
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording. "Thủ lĩnh" is the Kings word for sarim (2 Kings 24:12) and keeps the Hebrew's single word for human and heavenly princes; Readable says what the meaning decision says they are, as the English "ruling angel" does. The same words hold in 10:20-21 and 12:1.

decisions.choice: "Mi-ca-ên"
decisions.reason: The published form of Jude 9 and of the men named Michael in Chronicles.

sw.R: Sasa nimekuja kukusaidia uelewe yatakayowapata watu wako siku zijazo. Maono haya yanahusu wakati ambao bado haujafika."

decisions.choice: the end of the days: the days to come, the latter days
decisions.reason: The phrase means the future, often the time when God completes his purposes (Genesis 49:1; Isaiah 2:2; Daniel 2:28). Here it covers the events of chapter 11 and the end of 12:1-3.

decisions.choice: in the days to come (B); in the future (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the end of the days"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly. Literal's "there is still a vision for those days" follows the Hebrew word order.

decisions.choice: "trong những ngày cuối cùng" (L); "trong những ngày sắp tới" (B); "trong tương lai" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Isaiah 2:2 at each level, as the term sheet sets for "the latter days"; "thời kỳ cuối cùng" stays for "the time of the end" (8:17; 11:35).

decisions.choice: one in the likeness of the sons of man: one who looked human
decisions.reason: "Sons of man" means human beings. The phrase is a hedged description of a heavenly being in human form, like "one with the appearance of a man" in 8:15 and "one like a son of man" in 7:13. It is probably the same messenger as in verses 10-14.

decisions.choice: touched my lips: so that he could speak
decisions.reason: Compare Isaiah 6:7, where a seraph touches the prophet's lips, and Jeremiah 1:9. Daniel, struck dumb (verse 15), is enabled to speak.

decisions.choice: my lord: a polite address to a superior
decisions.reason: Daniel addresses the messenger as "my lord" (adoni), the respectful address used to a king or master (Genesis 24:18; 1 Samuel 25:24). It is not the title used for God.

decisions.choice: pangs: pains like those of childbirth
decisions.reason: The word is used of the pains of a woman in labor (1 Samuel 4:19; Isaiah 21:3). The vision has gripped Daniel with anguish.

decisions.choice: my lord (L, B); Sir (R); lowercase
decisions.reason: The address is lowercase, since it is said to a heavenly messenger (m3). Readable says "Sir", a polite address in plain English. Literal keeps "the sons of man"; Balanced and Readable say "a human being", as the table does for 7:13 at Readable.

decisions.choice: "mon seigneur", lowercase, at every level (R included)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets: "Monsieur" to an angel jars in French, and a capital would make "Seigneur" read as God.

decisions.choice: "[quelqu'un] semblable aux fils d'homme" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's "sons of man" without the article French uses for the Gospel title, as with "fils d'homme" in 8:17.

decisions.choice: "Mi señor" (L, B); "Señor" (R), lowercase inside a sentence
decisions.reason: Daniel's courteous address to the angel, with "tú"; it is never the capital "Señor" used for God, and at R it opens the sentence only by position

decisions.choice: "los hijos de los hombres" (L)
decisions.reason: As 2:38 L; the phrase already includes women and men, so it takes no gender span

decisions.choice: "Ee bwana wangu", lowercase, at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: Daniel's polite address to the angel is lowercase "bwana wangu" at every level, and "Ee" lets it open the sentence without a capital that would read as "Lord". The English Readable "Sir" is the same address.

decisions.choice: "thưa chúa tôi" (L, B); "thưa ngài" (R), lowercase, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Adoni is a polite address to a superior, as Joshua 5:14 "chúa tôi"; lowercase keeps it apart from "Chúa" for God. Daniel speaks of himself as "đầy tớ của chúa tôi" in verse 17. Readable's "ngài" is the respectful human word, not God's "Ngài".

decisions.choice: when I go out: when I have finished with Persia, or when I go out to battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to go out. It may mean that when the messenger leaves the fight with Persia, Greece's prince will come, as Greece followed Persia in history (8:20-21); or that when he goes out to battle, Greece's prince will come as well. The first fits the order of kingdoms in chapters 8 and 11.

decisions.choice: the prince of Persia, the prince of Greece: heavenly powers behind the nations
decisions.reason: As in verse 13. The struggle of nations on earth is shown with a struggle in heaven behind it.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruling angel (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruling angel" at Readable for the word sar where it names an angel. Readable says what kind of prince is meant, since a reader would otherwise think of a human prince; that the princes of Persia and Greece are angels is the usual reading but not certain (see the meaning decision at 10:13).

decisions.choice: the book of truth: the heavenly record of what God has decreed
decisions.reason: The "writing of truth" is the record of God's plan, which the messenger now reveals. Compare the books of 7:10 and 12:1, and the sealed scroll of Revelation 5:1.

decisions.choice: Michael, your prince: the heavenly protector of Daniel's people
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural: Michael is the prince of Daniel's people, Israel, as 12:1 says.

decisions.choice: the speech runs on into chapter 11
decisions.reason: The messenger's words continue in 11:1, where he says how he stood by Darius the Mede. The chapter break falls in the middle of his speech.

decisions.choice: the ruling angel who watches over your people (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "ruling angel" for prince, as the table gives, and says whose prince Michael is (m2). It capitalizes "Book of Truth" as a title.

decisions.choice: "votre prince" (L, B), plural "votre" for "your"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew suffix is plural: Michael is the prince of Daniel and his people. French "votre" shows that, where the English "your" cannot; Readable says "ton peuple".

decisions.choice: "el príncipe de ustedes" / "vuestro príncipe"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" is plural: Michael is the prince of Daniel's people, so it takes plural_you; "de ustedes" avoids the ambiguity of "su". R names the people, as the English R does

decisions.choice: no closing »
decisions.reason: The angel's speech runs on into chapter 11, as in the English

decisions.choice: "mkuu wenu", with the plural "wenu"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew suffix is plural: Michael is the prince of Daniel and his people. Swahili marks the plural, which English "your" cannot; Readable spells it out as "watu wako".

decisions.choice: "thủ lĩnh của các ông" (L); "thủ lĩnh của dân ông" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" is plural: Michael is the prince of Daniel's people, not of Daniel alone. Literal keeps the plural; Balanced says whose prince he is.
